steps.what: Read last year's syllabi and the homework assignments.
Decide how to prepare the course materials for this run.
Draft the syllabi, homework assignments and handouts she chose.

loop.input: The outcomes and session hours she wrote on the choice card in s2.
loop.output: Syllabus, homework and handout lines that quote those choices.
loop.check: Each line quotes an outcome or a session hour she wrote, and it adds no assessment she did not choose. A line that invents an outcome or an assessment fails.
loop.stop: One pass. A line that fails is dropped and is not repaired by a second invention. If every line fails, the card stays blank and she writes the pack.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot decide which outcome sentence belongs on which page of this run.

steps.what: Check each line quotes an outcome or hour she chose.
File the confirmed syllabi and handouts on the learning system.

tasks.design: She reads last year's pack and decides which outcomes and session hours this run will use. A loop drafts the syllabi, homework assignments and handouts by quoting only those choices onto an internal card. After she checks every line, a separate step files the confirmed pack on the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcomes are prose, so a blank form invents assessments she did not choose.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can quote only the outcomes and hours she chose, and drop a failing line.
tasks.still_hard: A new course, or a change in what is safe to teach, still needs her rewrite.
tasks.human_edge: She decides what this run will teach and which assessment is fair to set.

ambition.what: On every course run she maps each homework item to an outcome she chose, including runs where the pack is otherwise copied forward.

tasks.altitude: She still chooses the outcomes and still checks every line. The week loses the first draft of a stable pack and the filing, not the decision about what this run teaches.

reach.task: Publish the learning outcomes for this course
reach.learn: Which outcome sentences are stable enough to quote in a syllabus line.

evidence.claim: A draft that quotes only outcomes and hours she already chose is model knowledge. The digest does not name a product that writes this course pack.
Annex III covers evaluating learning outcomes. Drafting course materials is not that evaluation.

assumptions: The task ends when the confirmed pack is on the learning system. She does not grade here, and she does not mail the pack.

The programme coordinator produces the outcome sentences in {DOCS} before she reads them. The timetable owner produces the session hours. She copies the ones she chooses onto the choice card in s2 before the loop. If she chooses none, the loop does not run and the file step does not run.
Dutch examiner rules govern results, not syllabi. No staff-activity log is kept. Two hours per 100 baseline hours is deleting draft lines that quoted a retired outcome, beyond the check on that run.
The range is a new-course week against a stable run. Grading-time studies are not used.
unknowns: Whether this faculty also requires a programme-director sign-off before the learning system accepts the pack.
research_questions: How often a reused pack is rejected line by line because the outcomes changed?

already_counted.description: Checking that each draft line quotes an outcome or hour she chose.

incremental.description: Deleting draft lines that quoted a retired outcome, outside the check on that run.

approvals.approved_version: The confirmed pack from s4, bound to the outcomes and hours she chose in s2. A change to those choices voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A new-course week where she rewrites the pack during the check saves only the file step. A stable run saves part of the first draft. Two hours per 100 baseline hours is deleting draft lines that quoted a retired outcome, beyond that check. Grading-time studies are not used. High stays under the net of 42.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Name the field topics this current literature pass must cover.
Draft a card of developments that match those topics.

loop.input: The topic list she named in s1, and catalogue records that already carry a DOI or a catalogue id.
loop.output: A title card of developments whose titles match a topic she named.
loop.check: Each title's words match a topic she named, and the record resolves by DOI or catalogue id. A title that does not match her topic, or that does not resolve, is dropped. The check is the match to her topic, not only the identifier.
loop.stop: One pass. Do not invent a citation. If none resolve, the card stays empty and she picks papers herself.
loop.why_not_simpler: A keyword search does not know which topic she named for this pass.

steps.what: Check each title is current literature in that field.
Do the reading of the papers she kept.
Use the talking time with colleagues on those papers.
Keep abreast by participating in the professional conferences.

tasks.design: She names the field topics for this pass. A loop drafts a card of developments whose titles match those topics and resolve in the {OTHER} library catalogue. She checks the card, then does the reading, the talking with colleagues, and the professional conferences herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: An invented title list is worse than none, and a conference is not a document.
tasks.enabler_now: A catalogue id lets the check drop a title that does not resolve.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a paper changes what she teaches stays with her.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which paper changes the course, and she does the talking and the conference.
tasks.altitude: She still reads, still talks with colleagues and still attends the conferences. The week only loses the assembly of a title card she then checks.

reach.task: Keep the catalogue record and the DOI for a paper
reach.learn: Which index fields count as a resolved title.

evidence.claim: A named citation index suggests foundational papers for a topic. Here the result is a title card only, and she still reads the papers.
Invented references can pass a plagiarism check unflagged, so a title that does not resolve is dropped rather than trusted to a detector.
Referees may not use generative AI, and uploading a proposal breaches confidentiality. The card uses published catalogue records only.

assumptions: Reading, the colleague talk and the conference stay hers at full time. The card is internal. It is not sent and it is not an alert.

She produces the topic list in s1. The library catalogue produces the DOI or catalogue id before the loop reads it. The conference organiser produces the conference programme before she attends. Unpublished drafts and grant proposals are never the input.
No log is kept of what she reads. One hour per 100 baseline hours is retiring a topic outside the weekly pass. Some weeks no title resolves, so the low end of the range is zero.
unknowns: Which catalogue her library licenses for this field.
research_questions: What share of suggested titles fail the resolution check in her field?

already_counted.description: Checking that each title is current literature for a topic she named.

incremental.description: Retiring a topic outside the weekly literature pass.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Some weeks no title resolves, so the saving is zero. A week with a short card saves only that draft. Reading, colleague talk and the conferences stay at full time. One hour per 100 baseline hours is retiring a topic outside the weekly pass. High stays under the net of 7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Write the rubric and the key for this class work.
Read the students' class work, assignments and papers.
Score the closed items from the key she wrote.
Draft a group score and comment for similar open answers.

loop.input: The rubric and bands she wrote in s1, and the open answers she already read in s2.
loop.output: One internal group card: a suggested band and a comment for similar open answers.
loop.check: The comment quotes a rubric point she wrote, the suggested score is one of her bands, and the group contains only answers she read. A group that invents a student, or a comment that does not quote her rubric, is left unmarked.
loop.stop: One pass. A failed group is not repaired. The card is not written to either grade store.
loop.why_not_simpler: An exact match cannot judge an open answer.

steps.what: Evaluate and grade each student against the rubric.
File each confirmed grade on the learning-system column.
Copy each confirmed grade into the student-records field.

tasks.design: She writes the rubric and the closed-item key, and reads the scripts. One step scores closed items from that key onto an internal card, and a loop drafts one group score and comment for similar open answers, both of which she can reject when she grades. After she confirms every grade, one step files it on the {LMS} column and a second step copies that same confirmed value to the {OTHER} student-records field.
tasks.previous_blocker: A model-set grade would be the examiner's decision, and an open answer does not match a key.
tasks.enabler_now: Closed items can match the key she wrote, similar open answers can be grouped as a suggestion, and the two stores are keyed twice today.
tasks.still_hard: The grade and a fraud sanction stay with her and the examination board.
tasks.human_edge: She is the appointed examiner and she sets the result.
tasks.altitude: She still reads every script and still sets every grade. The week loses accepted closed-item keying and the two filings of a grade she already confirmed.

reach.task: Appoint the examiner for this course
reach.learn: That only the appointed examiner sets the grade, and the board alone sanctions fraud.

evidence.claim: Gradescope groups similar answers so a group can be reviewed together. The teacher still sets the grade. This range does not use the vendor time estimate.
Ans auto-marks closed questions and lists no AI feature. This step writes an internal card, not the stored grade.
One Dutch university requires the learning-system grade to be published again in the student-information system (Brightspace and OSIRIS).
The appointed examiner sets the result. Only the examination board sanctions fraud.
A grade set solely by a model is likely a solely automated decision, so the stored grade is the one she confirmed.
Evaluating learning outcomes is high-risk, and the grading duties apply from 2 December 2027. The draft score is not the grade.
One university forbids automated grading on EduGenAI, its staff chat platform.
Staff-monitoring systems need works-council consent, so this design keeps no per-examiner speed dashboard.

assumptions: She is the appointed examiner for this course. Fraud sanctions stay with the examination board and are not a step here. She does not message the grade.

She produces the rubric, the bands and the closed-item key in s1. The key is an exact stored choice, not a paraphrase. Students submit the answers before she reads them. The loop and the key match consume only those. A closed item with no key stays for her in the confirm step.

The closed-item card and the group card are not the grade column. Both stores receive only the confirmed value. The programme office owns the student-records field definition. If the institution has one store, the copy step does not run.

No per-examiner dashboard. A data-protection assessment for systematic grading support is a consent item, not a reason to let the model store the grade. Where the digest names the Dutch statute, the appointment rule applies. Elsewhere the person appointed to set the result confirms.
Two hours per 100 baseline hours is key maintenance when a question changes, outside the confirm pass. Published grading-time claims are not the range.
unknowns: Whether this institution has a second grade store.
Whether she is the appointed examiner for every course she teaches.
research_questions: What share of closed items have a stable key, and how often the second store exists?

already_counted.description: Evaluating and grading each student, including rejecting the closed-item card or the group card.

incremental.description: Key maintenance when a question changes, outside the confirm pass.

approvals.approved_version: The confirmed grade list from s5. A change to the rubric, the key or the answers voids this approval.
The same confirmed grade list from s5. A change to that list voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A paper week where she rewrites open comments during the confirm, and a second store exists, saves the closed-item keying plus the two filings. A week with no second store saves only the accepted closed-item marks. Two hours per 100 baseline hours is key maintenance when a question changes, outside the confirm pass. Published grading-time claims are not applied. High stays under the net of 36.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the laboratory session plan for this group.
Supervise the laboratory sessions in the room.
Correct a student's technique during the laboratory session.
Decide whether the laboratory work stays safe to continue.
Write the laboratory session note after the group leaves.

tasks.design: She reads the session plan, supervises the laboratory sessions in the room, corrects technique, and decides whether the work stays safe. She writes the session note herself after the group leaves. The design adds no machine step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The session is physical and the harm is immediate.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in the tools removes watching hands at the bench.
tasks.still_hard: An unsafe act is visible only when she is in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She sees an unsafe grip or a student who needs help and stops the bench.
tasks.altitude: The laboratory hour does not change. She still supervises, corrects technique, decides safety and writes the note.

reach.task: Set out the session's instruments and the safety steps
reach.learn: Which step she must not skip when the group arrives.

evidence.claim: Supervising a teaching laboratory is physical and situational. This design adds no bench-watching tool. That is model knowledge.
Emotion inference in education is prohibited. She supervises in the room and does not watch faces to infer emotion.
Staff-monitoring systems need works-council consent. A camera or a timing log would be that system, so none is added.

assumptions: The session is the room. Attendance filing is a different task and is not added here.
The laboratory technician produces the session plan and the safety steps before she reads the plan. The plan does not substitute for watching.
No camera, no remote halt, no emotion inference and no alert. Incremental hours are zero because there is no tool. The range is zero because no step is shortened.
unknowns: Which incidents the faculty requires in the session note.
research_questions: Which session hazards are visible only when she is at the bench?

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no steady-state upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. The session, the corrections, the safety decision and the note stay at full time. There is no tool, so incremental hours are zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still teaching, reading, grading and the laboratory. She still chooses the outcomes, reads the papers, talks with colleagues, attends the conferences, sets every grade and supervises the room. Only the draft pack, the title card, the closed-item scores and the two grade filings move.
reach: The programme coordinator keeps outcome sentences quotable in the course document.
The examination board appoints her as examiner and sanctions fraud.
The librarian keeps catalogue records, and an unresolved title is dropped.
The laboratory technician sets the safety steps before the group arrives.
skills_to_grow: Reject a syllabus line that adds an outcome or an assessment she did not choose.
Drop an unresolved title and still read the paper.
Set every grade herself, including a closed item and a group draft.
Supervise the laboratory without a camera or a remote halt.
role.ambitious_version: On a course run where the outcomes are stable, she confirms the draft pack once, and every student in that batch has a grade she set before either store keeps it.
